title: Claude Code
description: Usage, cost, tokens, tools and permissions for every Claude Code session that pushes OTLP to the local collector — the host's and every devbox container's. Reads all three signals: Prometheus for the counters, Loki for the event stream, Tempo for the spans. Metric names have no unit or _total suffix because the collector is configured with add_metric_suffixes: false. Several panels count with max_over_time rather than increase(); each says why in its own description.

list.name: workspace
list.label: Workspace
list.description: host, or a devbox checkout path. Filters every panel on the dashboard.

list.name: model
list.label: Model
list.description: Filters the cost and token panels. Panels whose metric has no model label ignore it.

list.name: session
list.label: Session
list.description: Drives the One session row. Listed as workspace + id, ordered by spend over the last 30 days, and filtered by the workspace variable. The name is the last segment of the workspace, which is a git repository on the host (host:dotfiles -> dotfiles) and a worktree in a devbox container. Claude Code does not export its session titles, so the id is the rest of the name.

panels.title: Sessions started
panels.description: Counts DISTINCT session_id, not increase(). Claude Code creates a session counter already holding 1 and it never moves again, so increase() measures a flat line and returns 0 at every range. max_over_time keeps the series alive across the window; count() then counts series, which is sessions.

panels.title: Cost
panels.description: max_over_time rather than increase() for the same reason as Sessions: the first sample of a session's counter is a step this dashboard would otherwise never see. The trade is that a session which started before the window contributes its whole total, not the part inside it.

panels.title: Cache read share
panels.description: Cache reads as a fraction of all tokens. Sits near 0.98 in normal use. A fall means the prompt cache is missing, and a cache miss is paid for at the full input rate.

panels.title: Net lines
panels.description: Added minus removed. A negative number is a refactor.

panels.title: Commits
panels.description: max_over_time, not increase(). increase() under-reports this counter by roughly half — it misses the step from the series being born.

panels.title: Tool calls
panels.description: From the Loki event stream, which is the only place tool calls are counted at all. The Prometheus side has a decision counter for Edit and Write and nothing for every other tool.

panels.title: Spend
panels.description: Where the money goes. Every panel here reads a label the cost counter already carries.

panels.title: Cost per hour, by model
panels.description: The rate of spend, not the total. Use the Spend per day panel below for 月 month-over-month comparison.

panels.title: Cost by query source
panels.description: main is your own prompts. subagent is everything an Agent call spawned. auxiliary is the background work — session titles, summaries, suggestions.

panels.title: Cost by effort
panels.description: What reaching for a higher effort level actually costs over the range.

panels.title: Spend per day
panels.description: Bars at one-day resolution. Set the dashboard range to a month or more and this is the panel the 100-year Prometheus retention exists for.

panels.title: Cost by workspace
panels.description: host is Claude Code on this machine. The rest are devbox worktrees, labelled by their checkout path.

panels.title: Cost by subagent
panels.description: Only samples that carry an agent_name — the rest is main-thread work.

panels.title: Cost by skill
panels.description: What each skill invocation cost. A skill that never appears here was never invoked in this range.

panels.title: Most expensive sessions
panels.description: session_id is a resume handle: claude --resume <id> reopens the session this row is about.

panels.title: Cost by MCP tool
panels.description: Thin until an MCP server does real work. Kept because an MCP round trip is the easiest cost to lose track of.

panels.title: Cache economics
panels.description: 98 of every 100 tokens are cache reads. On a linear stacked axis that hides the other three token types completely.

panels.title: Tokens by type
panels.description: Log-2 axis and NOT stacked, because cache reads outweigh output tokens by about 160 to 1. Stacked on a linear axis this panel is one flat band.

panels.title: Output tokens per dollar
panels.description: Writing produced per dollar spent, by model. Cache reads are excluded — they are input, and they are what makes the denominator small.

targets.expr: sum by (model) (max_over_time(claude_code_token_usage{workspace=~"$workspace", model=~"$model", type="output"}[$__range])) / sum by (model) (max_over_time(claude_code_cost_usage{workspace=~"$workspace", model=~"$model"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Cache writes per read
panels.description: cacheCreation over cacheRead. Around 0.015 in normal use — one write per 65 reads. A rise means the cache is being rebuilt instead of hit.

panels.title: Tokens, all types
panels.description: The denominator behind every ratio on this row.

panels.title: Cost per hour, by query source
panels.description: The same rate as the model panel above, split by who asked. auxiliary rising on its own is background work you did not request.

panels.title: Tool activity
panels.description: From the Loki event stream. Prometheus counts Edit and Write decisions and nothing else — everything on this row is unavailable on the metrics side.

panels.title: Tool calls by tool
panels.description: One count per tool_result event, which fires whether the call succeeded or not.

panels.title: Tool latency, p95 by tool
panels.description: duration_ms is structured metadata on the tool_result event, so it unwraps without a parser stage. WebFetch and WebSearch sit in the seconds; Read and Edit sit in the tens of milliseconds.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {service_name="claude-code", workspace=~"$workspace"} | event_name="tool_result" | unwrap duration_ms [$__auto]) by (tool_name)

panels.title: Tool failures
panels.description: A flat zero is the expected reading. Anything else names the tool that started failing and when.

panels.title: Prompts per interval
panels.description: One user_prompt event per prompt. The prompt TEXT is redacted unless OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS is set; the count and prompt_length arrive either way.

panels.title: Prompt length, p95
panels.description: prompt_length in characters. Tracks how much context you hand over by hand.

panels.title: Permission mode
panels.description: What the permission system decided, and which mode it was in when it decided. Read the caveat panel before trusting the source split.

panels.title: Permission mode changes
panels.description: One bar per permission_mode_changed event, by the mode being entered. Modes are default, plan, acceptEdits and auto.

panels.title: Mode transitions
panels.description: Which mode you leave for which. Records CHANGES only: a session that starts in a mode and stays there emits nothing, so this table cannot tell you what mode a session ran in.

panels.title: Tool grants by source
panels.description: config is a settings.json rule OR an auto-mode grant — the two are the same value. user_temporary and user_permanent are you, answering a prompt.

panels.title: Why there is no auto-mode count
panels.description: The caveat that makes the source split above readable.

options.content:
Claude Code exports **no metric for permission mode**. Two events carry the signal and neither closes the loop:

- `permission_mode_changed` fires on a **change**. A session that starts in `auto` emits nothing, so the mode a session ran in is not recoverable.
- `tool_decision` carries `source`, and an auto-mode grant writes the same `config` as a settings.json allowlist rule. The two cannot be told apart.

The one measure that does separate them is the `claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` span in Tempo — see the **Permission wait** row. It fires on every gate, auto-granted or not, and an auto-granted gate closes in ~15 ms where a gate you answered takes seconds. Duration is the discriminator.

panels.title: Accepts and rejects
panels.description: The whole decision stream over the range, one slice per decision and source pair.

panels.title: Rejections
panels.description: Decisions you refused, or a settings.json deny rule refused for you.

panels.title: Rejected tool calls
panels.description: The commands that were stopped. The line carries full_command because OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS is on in common/.zshrc — with it off, the event still arrives but names no command.

panels.title: Session shape
panels.description: How a session begins, how the time inside it splits, and what it leaves in the repository.

panels.title: Fresh, resume or continue
panels.description: count of DISTINCT sessions per start_type. increase() returns 0 here for the reason described on the Sessions started panel.

panels.title: Claude working
panels.description: active_time type=cli: seconds Claude spent working, over the range.

panels.title: You working
panels.description: active_time type=user: seconds you spent typing. The ratio against the panel to the left is the leverage this whole stack exists to measure.

panels.title: Active time
panels.description: Seconds of work per second of wall clock. Above 1 means concurrent sessions.

panels.title: Lines of code
panels.description: Added and removed per interval, from the edit tools rather than from git.

panels.title: Edits by language
panels.description: From the Edit and Write decision counter, which is the only Prometheus metric that knows what a file contained.

panels.title: Harness health
panels.description: The parts of the machine around the model: hooks, MCP servers, subagents and skills. Hook events outnumber every other event type in the store.

panels.title: Hook runs by hook
panels.description: Two per Bash call in a normal configuration — one PreToolUse, one PostToolUse. These run on the critical path of every tool use.

panels.title: Hook latency, p95
panels.description: total_duration_ms per hook_name. This is the panel that catches a hook that got slow and started taxing every tool call.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {service_name="claude-code", workspace=~"$workspace"} | event_name="hook_execution_complete" | unwrap total_duration_ms [$__auto]) by (hook_name)

panels.title: Hook errors
panels.description: hook_execution_complete events where a hook reported a non-blocking error. Expected reading is zero.

panels.title: Blocking hook stops
panels.description: A blocking hook refused a tool call. Rare and worth reading the log for.

panels.title: MCP server connections
panels.description: server_name, status and how long the handshake took. A server that is slow to start delays the session start behind it.

targets.expr: sum by (server_name, status, transport_type) (count_over_time({service_name="claude-code", workspace=~"$workspace"} | event_name="mcp_server_connection" [$__range]))

panels.title: Subagent runs
panels.description: Expand a line for agent_type, duration_ms, total_tokens, total_tool_uses and model_swapped — the whole record of what a subagent did with its time.

panels.title: Skill activations
panels.description: invocation_trigger separates a slash command from claude-proactive, which is the answer to whether a skill's description is doing its job.

panels.title: API health
panels.description: The api_request event knows 19 query sources where the cost metric knows 3, and it carries its own cost, duration and token counts.

panels.title: API calls by true source
panels.description: repl_main_thread is your prompts. Everything else — sdk, agent:builtin:Explore, generate_session_title, away_summary, prompt_suggestion, web_search_tool — is work the metric label collapses into main and auxiliary.

panels.title: API latency, p95 by model
panels.description: Wall time of the API call itself, from the event rather than from a span.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {service_name="claude-code", workspace=~"$workspace"} | event_name="api_request" | unwrap duration_ms [$__auto]) by (model)

panels.title: API errors
panels.description: api_error and api_retries_exhausted together. A panel worth having at zero — it is the only place a failed call is recorded.

panels.title: Cost per API call, p95
panels.description: The tail cost of one turn. cost_usd is on the event; cost_usd_micros is beside it if the float precision ever matters.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {service_name="claude-code", workspace=~"$workspace"} | event_name="api_request" | unwrap cost_usd [$__auto]) by (model)

panels.title: Permission wait
panels.description: From Tempo. Needs the metrics_generator block in tempo/tempo.yml — without it every panel here answers 'empty ring'. Counts start from the moment the generator was enabled, not from the start of retention.

panels.title: Permission gates per second
panels.description: One blocked_on_user span per gate, auto-granted or not.

panels.title: Gates that reached you, p95 wait
panels.description: Filtered to gates slower than a second, which is the threshold that separates an auto grant (~15 ms) from a prompt you actually answered.

panels.title: Time to first token, p95 by model
panels.description: ttft_ms lives on the llm_request span and nowhere else in this stack — neither Prometheus nor Loki carries it.

panels.title: Interaction duration, p95
panels.description: The root span: one per prompt, covering every API call and tool call nested under it.

panels.title: One session
panels.description: Everything above, narrowed to the session picked in the $session variable. Set it from the Most expensive sessions table.

panels.title: Session cost
panels.description: The whole session's spend, whatever the dashboard range.

panels.title: Session tokens
panels.description: All four token types together.

panels.title: Session tool calls
panels.description: From the event stream, so every tool counts and not only the edit tools.

panels.title: Session prompts
panels.description: user_prompt events in the session.

panels.title: Session cost per hour, by model
panels.description: Where the session's money went, over its own lifetime.

panels.title: Session events
panels.description: Every event the session emitted, newest first. The TraceID field on a line opens the trace in Tempo.
